tip: Spain's NIE appointment system (Sede Electrónica) releases new slots every Monday at 8am. Set an alarm!
The Padrón (town hall registration) is free and takes 10 minutes. Bring your passport, rental contract, and landlord's NIE.
Spanish banks often require 3 months of Padrón history to open an account. N26 or Wise are faster alternatives while you wait.
Your NIE and TIE are different. The NIE is your tax number, the TIE is your physical residence card. You need both.
Healthcare tip: Register at your local Centro de Salud within 30 days of getting your TIE to get your Tarjeta Sanitaria.
The Digital Nomad Visa allows you to apply for the Beckham Law — a flat 24% tax rate on Spanish income for 6 years.
Most Spanish consulates require documents to be less than 90 days old at the time of your appointment. Plan accordingly.
FBI background checks take 12-18 weeks by mail but only 3-5 days through an approved FBI channeler. Worth the extra cost.
Idealista is Spain's #1 rental site, but beware of scams. Never pay before visiting in person or through a verified agent.
Spanish pharmacies (farmacias) can give basic medical advice and sell many medications over the counter that require prescriptions elsewhere.
Get your NIF (tax number) before arriving — services like Bordr.io can do it remotely for about €150.
Portugal's D7 visa is the most popular for Americans. You need proof of passive income equal to Portugal's minimum wage (~€820/month).
AIMA (formerly SEF) appointments can take months. Book as soon as you arrive — don't wait.
ActivoBank is the easiest Portuguese bank for expats — no monthly fees and online-friendly.
Portugal's NHR (Non-Habitual Resident) tax regime offers reduced rates for 10 years. Apply within the first year of becoming tax resident.
Register at your local Junta de Freguesia (parish council) within 3 days of signing a rental contract.
Portuguese health centers (Centro de Saúde) provide free primary care once you're registered with SNS.
Lisbon and Porto have excellent public transport. Consider a monthly Navegante pass (€40) — unlimited metro, bus, tram, and trains.
Portugal's Golden Visa program changed in 2023 — real estate no longer qualifies. Fund investments start at €500K.
Portuguese rental contracts are typically 1 year minimum. Furnished apartments are rare — most rentals come empty.
Mexico's Temporary Resident visa doesn't require a background check — just financial proof. One of the simplest visa processes.
You have exactly 30 days after entering Mexico to exchange your visa sticker for a Resident Card at INM. Don't miss this deadline.
IMSS Voluntario (public health insurance) costs about $500/year and covers you at any IMSS hospital. Great value for basic coverage.
Your CURP is automatically generated when you get your INM card. You can also look it up at curp.gob.mx.
Mexican consulates often accept walk-ins for visa appointments. But calling ahead to confirm is always smart.
BBVA México has the best English-language app and is the most expat-friendly bank. Bring your resident card, CURP, and proof of address.
Mexico uses CFE for electricity. Bills arrive every 2 months. Set up autopay at cfe.mx to avoid late fees.
San Miguel de Allende has the largest US expat community in Mexico. Mérida is the safest city. Playa del Carmen has the best nightlife.
Get a Mexican phone number immediately — Telcel has the best coverage. Most plans are prepaid and very affordable (~$10/month).
If you earn income while in Mexico, you need an RFC (tax ID) from SAT. Remote workers for foreign companies often overlook this.
Apostilles can take 4-8 weeks. Start this process as early as possible — it's the most common cause of visa delays.
Make digital copies of every document before your move. Store them in Google Drive or iCloud — you'll need them more than you think.
Wise (formerly TransferWise) consistently offers the best exchange rates for international transfers. Set up your account before you move.
Join Facebook expat groups for your target city before you move. They're goldmines for apartment leads, recommendations, and local knowledge.
Always keep your original documents AND certified copies separate. If your luggage is lost, you'll still have one set.
